findings.claim: The observed score clock spans 0.0 to 0.49 in 50 evenly spaced nodes and the learning window is [0.0, 0.5]; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so selection preference is the only available label and decoded final affinity is unobserved.
The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate proxies are therefore not themselves the objective.

The landmark_00_soft_mass curve over the full observed support is non-monotone: it rises from a negative early value to a mid-window maximum and then declines to a negative late value, with first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative, 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict across 14 independent batches; the cubic polynomial was not accepted and extrapolation is disallowed.

hypotheses.direction: non-monotone; early positive rate, late negative rate
hypotheses.falsifier: A re-read of the same curve over the same support showing a single consistent sign of the rate with no strong sign conflict, or an accepted polynomial fit with a stable profile.
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: landmark_00_soft_mass exhibits a rising-then-falling contrast across the observed score window, so any reward tracking this coordinate should be evaluated as a time-varying contrast rather than a fixed absolute target.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves and summary tables were accessible.
Only landmark_00_soft_mass was read as an actual curve; other landmark coordinates were not inspected, so no cross-landmark comparison is claimed.
Decoded final affinity labels are unobserved (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so no statement about descendant survival or measured final benefit is supported.
The observed trend is a selection-association contrast, not evidence of a reward effect; no dose or reward intervention has been evaluated here.
